g.text: Input frequency + duty meter - the protocol engine on both sides
the pin is an INPUT; the claim is the accuracy of a COUNT, not a delay
FIRMWARE SIDE - firmware/freqmeter.pe
POLL
read the 1 us COUNTER (port 4, I2CTICK),
NOT the flag and NOT port 7
(see the timebase note below)
ELAPSED
(now - previous) mod 256
dmem[7] holds the previous reading.
THERE IS NO FLAG TO LOSE
, so a slow
iteration - and the BANK below is the
slowest thing in the program - makes the
measurement LATE BY EXACTLY THE RIGHT
AMOUNT rather than wrong.
this loop is 1.3 us: two hundred times
inside the 255 us the subtraction is
exact for.
AND THE SUBTRACTION NEEDS NO CARRY TEST:
the
borrow of (previous - now) is only ever used
as "is it zero", which is the ONE comparison
the ISA has. One SUB does both jobs: the
borrow IS the comparison, and the value IS
the elapsed time.
ADD
into H, and into T
the addend is the elapsed time, which is
NEVER ZERO, so "the low byte came out zero"
can only mean "the low byte WRAPPED" and the
high byte must be incremented. No both-zero
guard is needed - a program adding two memory
values would need it, because 0 + 0 = 0 is
not a carry.
THERE IS NO 16-BIT SUBTRACT AND NO COMPARE IN THIS
PROGRAM, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN - not a limitation
worked around.
PAD
changed?
dmem[4] holds the previous pad level
(00 or 40). IN A, PIN; AND A, FM_IN.
RISING
reset both counters
T (dmem[0..1]) = 0 - the period counter
H (dmem[2..3]) = 0 - the high-time counter
THIS ONE DESIGN DECISION REMOVES EVERY 16-BIT
SUBTRACT, EVERY COMPARE AND EVERY DIVIDE:
the period is T at the RISING edge, because T is
RESET at every rising edge; the high time is H at
the RISING edge, because H is also reset there and
STOPS COUNTING at the falling edge.
The commit message called this act "capture only"
before a line of it existed, and that is what it
turned out to be, for a reason the commit message
could not have known.
FALLING
stop H
H stops counting here. Nothing to subtract:
the accumulator simply stops.
BANK
a 16-bit pair
every 3 periods, (T, H) is banked into the
slot dmem[5] names, and dmem[5] advances.
THE FIRST PERIOD OF EACH RUN IS A WARM-UP AND IS
NOT CHECKED, for a reason that is a property of
the PROTOCOL and not of the firmware: the
firmware starts in the middle of it, so the time
since the previous rising edge is not a period.
A receiver that starts mid-period misses that
one period, and a testbench that pretended
otherwise would be asking the firmware to
measure something it was never present for.
DONE
dmem[6] = 1 when both slots are banked.
dmem[5] DOUBLES AS THE "NOT STARTED YET" STATE
(FF), because the program needed one byte more
than the machine has and the slot index is the
one value that is not a measurement.
GENERATOR + RECEIVER - tb/tb_pe_soc_freqmeter.v
SWEEP
6 runs of 3 periods, 18 driven periods,
12 banked points,
158 Hz to 10 000 Hz
with a varying duty
THE GENERATOR IS EDGE-DRIVEN WITH ABSOLUTE
DELAYS, not woken once per clock: a 2.6 M
clock TB that woke up 2.6 M times to decide
whether the pin had moved would spend its wall
time deciding it had not.
RECEIVE
an independent measurement
the receiver measures the pad with its
OWN edge logic, and the firmware's banked
values are checked against THAT - not against
the generator's table.
A generator that knew
the answer would agree with a firmware that had
the sweep wrong.
CHECK
what is claimed
1. every banked period is within 1 % of
the pad's period, with a floor of 1.5 ticks
2. every banked high time likewise
3. the duty follows
4. the DONE flag is set, and every result was
ACTUALLY WRITTEN
5. the twelve periods are pairwise DISTINCT
6. the twelve duties are neither constant nor
50 % twice running
7. at least one banked period is above 255 while
another is inside a byte - the 16-bit claim
stated from BOTH sides
Why the tolerance is per point and not one number.
The instrument's resolution IS the specification, and
a single accuracy figure would be a false claim at one
end or the other:
point
period
error of a 1 us counter
100 us (10 kHz)
So the tolerance is 1 % of the period with a floor of
1.5 ticks: at the fast end of the sweep the TOLERANCE
is the dominant term and the quantisation is a percent
of it.
THE TIMEBASE TRAP, and why the flag is not used
either. This SoC has TWO tick counters and they are
not the same size.
port
name
period
what it is for
STATUS
260 clocks =
the UART half-bit tick: it exists to place a serial sample mid-cell
I2CTICK
60 clocks =
1 us
the free-running microsecond counter
I2CSTAT
1 us
that counter's clear-on-read FLAG
The first version counted STATUS, and measured
0.24 ticks per microsecond
: a factor of 4.33 out,
reporting a 200 us period as 46. A tick counter whose
name says TIMER is not a microsecond.
And the flag is not the fix. A clear-on-read flag is ONE
BIT, so a poll loop that takes longer than a tick
reports several ticks as one, and the loss is invisible
in the result - the measurement is simply short, by an
amount that depends on how busy the program was. This
program is one instruction from that defect and does not
have it, because it reads the COUNTER and adds the
DIFFERENCE.
THE MACHINE HAS SIXTEEN BYTES, AND THE
TESTBENCH HAD TO BE TOLD.
A period is two bytes and a high time two, so the
firmware banks TWO POINTS PER RUN and the sweep is SIX
RUNS OF THREE PERIODS.
The RED testbench had asked for sixteen points in
dmem[0..63] on a machine with sixteen bytes: twelve of
its own expectations were read out of an address space
that does not exist, and its DONE flag at dmem[14] was
INSIDE THE DATA IT WAS REPORTING.
A test that sizes memory to what it wishes for is a
test that reports success without measuring anything,
and the count of such elements in this block is now
three.
the level CHANGED, to high
the level CHANGED, to low
no change: keep counting
every third period
both slots banked
